newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to sell off 10 pct of Helwan.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to sell off 10 pct of Helwan.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories said on Monday it was offering to investors at least 2.5 million shares, or 10 percent, of Helwan Portland Cement.
The partial privatisation, the agents for which are Misr Exterior Bank and the securities group EFG-Hermes, will be by auction, the company said in a published statement.
Bids must be for at least 25,000 shares and the minimum price for each share is 56.50 pounds, which was the closing price on November 21 on the Cairo bourse.

The parent company will accept the bids in sealed envelopes between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. on Wednesday, November 27. The bid must be accompanied by a bank cheque or guarantee for two percent of the value of the bid.
Individuals, mutual funds and financial institutions currently hold 29.8 percent of Helwan Cement. The holding company retains 70.2 percent.

Helwan Cement increased net profits for financial year 1995/96 to 125.52 million pounds ($36.9 million) from 103.61 million a year earlier. The financial year ended on June 30. Net profits in the first quarter of 96/97 were 35 million pounds.

The firm, one of Egypt's leading cement manufacturers, said earlier this month it was raising dividends for 1995/96 to five pounds from the 4.75 pounds it had promised investors earlier this year. Dividends for 1994/95 were four pounds per share.
The firm's net sales rose to 550.57 million pounds from 495.73 million in 1994/95.
